items.informal_name: Lower Bound on Weighted Order of Multivariate Power Series
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] (w : σ → ℕ) {f : MvPowerSeries σ R} {n : ℕ∞},
  (∀ (d : σ →₀ ℕ), ↑((Finsupp.weight w) d) < n → (MvPowerSeries.coeff d) f = 0) → n ≤ MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w f
items.informal_description: For any extended natural number $n$, if every monomial $d$ with $\text{weight}(w, d) < n$ has zero coefficient in the multivariate power series $f$, then $n \leq \text{weightedOrder}(f, w)$, where $\text{weightedOrder}(f, w)$ denotes the weighted order of $f$ with respect to the weight function $w$.

items.informal_name: Weighted Order Lower Bound for Multivariate Power Series
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] (w : σ → ℕ) {f : MvPowerSeries σ R} {n : ℕ},
  (∀ (d : σ →₀ ℕ), (Finsupp.weight w) d < n → (MvPowerSeries.coeff d) f = 0) → ↑n ≤ MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w f
items.informal_description: For a multivariate power series $ f $ over a semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $ and a weight function $ w : \sigma \to \mathbb{N} $, if every monomial $ d $ with weighted sum $ \sum_{i \in \text{support } d} w(i) \cdot d(i) < n $ has zero coefficient in $ f $, then the weighted order of $ f $ with respect to $ w $ satisfies $ n \leq \text{weightedOrder}_w(f) $.

items.informal_name: Weighted Order Upper Bound for Multivariate Power Series
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] (w : σ → ℕ) {f : MvPowerSeries σ R} {d : σ →₀ ℕ},
  (MvPowerSeries.coeff d) f ≠ 0 → MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w f ≤ ↑((Finsupp.weight w) d)
items.informal_description: For a multivariate power series $ f $ over a semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $ and a weight function $ w : \sigma \to \mathbb{N} $, if the coefficient of a monomial $ d $ in $ f $ is non-zero, then the weighted order of $ f $ is less than or equal to the weight of $ d $, i.e., $ \operatorname{weightedOrder}_w(f) \leq \sum_{i \in \operatorname{support} d} w(i) \cdot d(i) $.

items.informal_name: Degree Bound for Multivariate Polynomials in Chevalley's Theorem
items.type: ℕ → (ℕ → ℕ) → ℕ → ℕ
items.informal_description: A function that computes a degree bound for multivariate polynomials, taking a natural number $n$, a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and an element of the sum type $\mathbb{N} \oplus \mathbb{N}$. For left components, it applies $f$ to $n$, and for right components, it returns $n$ directly. This is used in the proof of Chevalley's theorem to establish well-founded recursion for multivariate polynomial constructions.

items.informal_name: Weighted Monomial Degree ≤ Weighted Total Degree
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] {σ : Type u_3} [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M]
  [inst_2 : SemilatticeSup M] [inst_3 : OrderBot M] (w : σ → M) {φ : MvPolynomial σ R} {d : σ →₀ ℕ},
  d ∈ φ.support → (Finsupp.weight w) d ≤ MvPolynomial.weightedTotalDegree w φ
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $\varphi$ over a commutative semiring $R$ with variables indexed by $\sigma$, any weighting function $w : \sigma \to M$ where $M$ is a sup-semilattice, and any monomial $d$ in the support of $\varphi$, the weight of $d$ with respect to $w$ is less than or equal to the weighted total degree of $\varphi$ with respect to $w$.

items.informal_name: Positivity of Degree Bound in Chevalley's Theorem
items.type: ∀ (k : ℕ) (D : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ), 0 < ChevalleyThm.MvPolynomialC.degBound k D n
items.informal_description: For any natural number $k$ and function $D : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the degree bound $\text{degBound}\,k\,D\,n$ satisfies $0 < \text{degBound}\,k\,D\,n$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

items.type:

  MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w ((MvPowerSeries.monomial d) a) = if a = 0 then ⊤ else ↑((Finsupp.weight w) d)

items.informal_name: Coefficients of Multivariate Power Series with Weight Below Weighted Order Are Zero
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] (w : σ → ℕ) {f : MvPowerSeries σ R} {d : σ →₀ ℕ},
  ↑((Finsupp.weight w) d) < MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w f → (MvPowerSeries.coeff d) f = 0
items.informal_description: For a multivariate power series $ f $ over a semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $ and a weight function $ w : \sigma \to \mathbb{N} $, if the weighted sum $ \sum_{i \in \text{support } d} w(i) \cdot d(i) $ of a monomial $ d $ is strictly less than the weighted order of $ f $, then the coefficient of $ d $ in $ f $ is zero. The weighted order of $ f $ is defined as the minimal natural number $ n $ such that there exists a monomial with non-zero coefficient in $ f $ whose weighted sum equals $ n $. If $ f $ is the zero series, its weighted order is $ \top $ (infinity).

items.informal_name: Total Degree in Variable Less Than d iff All Monomials Have Exponents Less Than d
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : σ} {f : MvPolynomial σ R} {d : ℕ},
  0 < d → (MvPolynomial.degreeOf n f < d ↔ ∀ m ∈ f.support, m n < d)
items.informal_description: For a multivariate polynomial $ f $ over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $, the total degree of $ f $ in variable $ n $ is less than $ d $ if and only if every monomial in the support of $ f $ has an exponent of $ n $ strictly less than $ d $. Here, the support of $ f $ denotes the finite set of monomials (represented as finite support functions $ \sigma \to_0 \mathbb{N} $) with non-zero coefficients in $ f $.

items.informal_name: Degree of Variable in Polynomial ≤ d iff All Monomials Have Degree ≤ d
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : σ} {f : MvPolynomial σ R} {d : ℕ},
  MvPolynomial.degreeOf n f ≤ d ↔ ∀ m ∈ f.support, m n ≤ d
items.informal_description: For a multivariate polynomial $ f $ over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $, and for a variable $ n \in \sigma $ and a natural number $ d $, the degree of $ n $ in $ f $ is less than or equal to $ d $ if and only if every monomial in the support of $ f $ has the exponent of $ n $ less than or equal to $ d $.

items.informal_name: Component of Finite Support Function is Bounded by Its Degree
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_5} [inst : AddCommMonoid R] [inst_1 : PartialOrder R] [CanonicallyOrderedAdd R] (s : σ)
  (f : σ →₀ R), f s ≤ Finsupp.degree f
items.informal_description: For any element $s$ in $\sigma$ and any finite support function $f : \sigma \to_0 R$ (where $R$ is an additive commutative monoid equipped with a partial order and canonical order structure), the value $f(s)$ is less than or equal to the degree of $f$, defined as the sum of $f(i)$ over all $i$ in the support of $f$.

items.informal_name: Support Exponents are Bounded by Polynomial Degree
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Semiring R] {p : Polynomial R}, ∀ a ∈ p.support, ↑a ≤ p.degree
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ over a semiring $ R $, if a natural number $ a $ is in the support of $ p $, then $ a \leq \deg(p) $.

items.informal_name: Infimum degree of an element in the additive monoid algebra
items.type:
{R : Type u_1} →
  {A : Type u_3} →
    {T : Type u_4} →
      [inst : Semiring R] → [inst_1 : SemilatticeInf T] → [OrderTop T] → (A → T) → AddMonoidAlgebra R A → T
items.informal_description: For an element $ f $ in the additive monoid algebra $ R[A] $, this function computes the infimum (greatest lower bound) of the degrees of the elements in its support, where the support consists of the non-zero terms of $ f $. The infimum is taken with respect to the degree ordering $ D $ on the additive monoid $ A $, starting from the top element and iteratively combining with the degrees of each term in the support.

items.informal_name: Exponent in Support is at Most Natural Degree
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Semiring R] {p : Polynomial R}, ∀ a ∈ p.support, a ≤ p.natDegree
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ over a semiring and any natural number $ a $, if $ a $ is in the support of $ p $ (i.e., the exponent of a non-zero term in $ p $), then $ a $ is less than or equal to the natural degree of $ p $, denoted $ \operatorname{natDegree} p $.

items.type:
